messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED — Elevated 5xxs and latency observed in ca-central-1 affecting Hosted API endpoints and several Dedicated pools. Pager sent to oncall.
michelle: seeing large spike in 5xx across /v1/completions in ca-central-1. Error mix looks like 503/504 + STS token errors. Rate of errors ~12%. :rotating_light:
jason: confirmed. Auth token errors from AWS STS for several hosts in the dedicated pool — `GetCallerIdentity` failing with 500s and intermittent timeouts. ELB also shows surge in 502/503s.
kate: Datadog shows ingest lag for traces from ca-central-1 ~3m, but metrics still flowing. Honeycomb traces are sparse (maybe vendor ingest). This makes root cause harder to trace.
luis: customers on dedicated in ca-central-1 reporting higher latency and retries. Support queue rising. I pushed an initial status to #support-private and escalated to support-alejandra.
oncall-pager: I’m on it. Paging SRE now. Setting incident severity to SEV2 until mitigations are in place.
michelle: immediate asks — (1) Can we route Hosted API traffic away from ca-central-1 to healthy region? (2) Can Dedicated pools fall back to alternate region or spin up capacity?
jason: working on routing. Control plane accepts region fallback override. I’ll try a soft-failover for read traffic first, leave pinned customers alone unless they opt in. Command I’m using:
```
POST https://controlplane.api/redwood/v1/routing/override
{
  "from_region": "ca-central-1",
  "to_region": "us-east-1",
  "mode": "soft-failover",
  "scope": "hosted*"
}
```
michelle: +1. Set conservative throttle so we don’t swamp us-east-1. Also enable automatic model-variant fallback for pinned customers.
kate: also toggled trace sampling back up for us-east-1 so we can get better telemetry post-failover. Datadog alert updated to ignore transient error bursts for 10m.
deploy-bot: config-change: routing-override -> applied by jason (id: cfg-9921). No deploys in flight.
jason: routing change applied. Initial metrics show 35% of ca-central-1 traffic routed to us-east-1. Latency for those requests normalizing ~800ms -> 180ms. 5xx rate for hosted endpoints down to 6% overall.
luis: support-alejandra started outbound to top 12 affected customers with targeted mitigations and ETA. Templates: short impact + mitigation + recommended client-side retry window.
support-alejandra: posted to status.redwood.ai (maintenances) and added note: "Customers in ca-central-1 may see elevated latency/5xx; we are routing traffic to alternate regions. If you have pinned region requirements, contact support for assisted failover."
oncall-pager: next mitigation: scale up Dedicated capacity in fallback region for customers who opt in. @eng-ops please prepare capacity.
michelle: eng-ops (kate) — can we spin up extra g4dn pools in us-east-1 and us-west-2? Need enough to cover high-CPU inference jobs.
kate: spinning up additional dedicated pools now. ETA ~12–18 minutes for instance allocation + warmup. Will prioritize customers flagged critical.
jason: small note — AWS STS errors appear correlated with a broader control-plane degradation in ca-central-1 (API gateway latencies). Filing AWS support case and opening a ticket with their infrastructure team. Case #1234567890.
luis: noticed some retries causing an amplification of requests to STS from proxies; added local caching of STS tokens on proxies to reduce calls (per runbook step 4). Patch applied to proxy fleet in ca-central-1: `sts_cache_ttl=300s`.
michelle: good. Put a temporary circuit breaker for heavy customers making repetitive token requests: config snippet below.
```
circuit_breaker:
  max_calls_per_minute: 600
  penalty_window: 60
```
deploy-bot: rollback: autoscaler config change from earlier today was rolled back in ca-central-1 to reduce flapping (id: cfg-9917).
jason: AWS replied acknowledging elevated control-plane error rate in ca-central-1; they’re investigating ELB and STS. They flagged it as "service disruption" on their side. Link: https://status.aws.amazon.com/incidents/CA-CENTRAL-1-XYZ
oncall-pager: need to capture timeline and actions for postmortem. @michelle can you own the incident timeline?
michelle: I’ll own timeline + postmortem. Please drop short notes in this thread. I’ll compile.
support-alejandra: customers want ETA for full recovery — we should provide conservative estimate: 2–6 hours given AWS remediation and pool warmups. I’ll update status page.
jason: handover note — I’m going offline in ~30m. @kate will be primary SRE for continued mitigation and monitoring. Leaving runbook steps performed: routing override, sts_cache, proxy patch, dedicated pool spin-up request, customer comms.
kate: ack taking lead. I’ll watch error budget and scaling metrics. If AWS fixes control plane, we can re-route back and drain fallback region.
luis: tracking support tickets: #SR-8341, #SR-8342, #SR-8349 — bumping priority for enterprise customers.
michelle: make sure billing/usage is noted for customers who had to use cross-region capacity — finance might need a credit plan. @finance please standby.
oncall-pager: set reminder for 3am UTC for follow-up check and meet for handoff to night oncall.
michelle: adding notes: suspected root cause = AWS control-plane API (ELB/ST S) partial outage in ca-central-1 causing token failures -> proxy retries -> amplification -> elevated 5xx. Contributing factor = observability ingest lag (Datadog/Honeycomb) made early detection harder.
deploy-bot: incident-log: routing-override by jason at 2387654400, proxy-patch by luis at 2387654800, support-notice by support-alejandra at 2387655100.
kate: markers: if 5xx drops below 1% for 30m and end-to-end latency normalizes, we do controlled failback: (1) reduce override to 10% -> (2) observe 15m -> (3) fully revert.
michelle: handing off to @kate for active monitoring and next steps. I’ll continue timeline and start the postmortem draft once incident stabilizes.
support-alejandra: will continue customer comms and collect impacted customer logs for RCA.
oncall-pager: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity remains SEV2. Keep this thread for live notes. Handoff to night oncall complete.
